svg.title: Five layers of failure handling in a cloud flow
svg.desc: A failure passes through five layers, from the inside out. Layer 1, the action's retry policy: repeats the request for transient failures only (408, 429, 5xx, time-outs); a 400 from a plug-in or a 403 is not retried. Layer 2, run after: the next action accepts Failed and TimedOut and handles the failure of one action. Layer 3, scopes: Try groups the work, Catch runs after Try has failed or timed out and reads result('Try'), and a finally action runs after Catch with all four statuses. Layer 4, the verdict: Terminate with status Failed makes the run show what happened, because a failure that was handled otherwise ends as Succeeded. Layer 5, outside the run: the alert sent by the handler, the run history with Resubmit, the platform's mails to the owner, and the rule that a flow failing for 14 days is turned off. A side panel shows the status trap with three small graphs: handler only, the run succeeds; handler plus a skipped normal path, the run fails; both paths joined in one end that accepts Succeeded and Skipped, the run succeeds.
svg.text: A failure travels outwards until a layer deals with it
Repeats the request for transient failures: 408, 429, 5xx, time-outs.
Not retried: 400 from a plug-in rule, 401, 403, 404. Types: Default, None,
“has failed” and “has timed out” ticked: this action is the handler
of one predecessor. Otherwise everything after a failure is Skipped.
Try: the work. Its status is Failed when anything inside failed.
Catch: runs after Try has failed or timed out; result('Try') lists the
top-level actions of Try with status, inputs, outputs, error.
Finally: runs after Catch with all four statuses (the response, the clean-up).
A handled failure ends as Succeeded. End the handler with Terminate, status
Failed, code and message, so that the run history tells the truth.
The alert the handler sent (Cedar: one child flow for all flows).
Run history, 30 days: open the run, Resubmit, Cancel.
The platform's mails to the flow owner; a flow that fails or is throttled
continuously is turned off after 14 days.
Later: Application Insights for all flows (lesson 105).
b) Handler and a normal path
A skipped end counts as its predecessor.
c) One end for both paths
Done runs after Succeeded or Skipped
Dashed red line = run after “has failed”.
